_comment: DRAFT narration for p348 (source: js/data/batch-10.js, author agatha). Original text is kept; emoji are display-only and never spoken. Teach words: accused (base 'accuse'), witness, guilty. 'suspect' and 'indicted' are read normally, no handoff. 'patron' and 'witnessSent' are ONE sentence each, interrupted by a vocabulary note (one take, cut after the teach word). 'But a witness — me — saw everything.' is written with commas here: the em dashes would become word-less display tokens that the reading cue shows as active for the whole line (ReadingCue is frozen). The 'hook' segment is the chosen scene_contrast candidate A. Vocabulary meanings / examples are the real entries from js/data/batch-10.js (accuse, witness, guilty). 'accusedRest' uses cut: "late": the final /d/ of 'accused' is released into 'of', so the default quietest-point cut left the /d/ burst at the start of the second part (heard as 'the returning'). KNOWN LIMITATION: display-only punctuation (here the em dashes) has no punctuation mapping in the reading cue yet; this episode uses the comma version.

segments.text: One coffee stain on a library book. Now it's a court case.
Library Court is now in session.
A patron was accused of returning a book with a coffee stain.
She accused her brother of eating her cake.
The suspect said he was innocent.
But a witness, me, saw everything.
A witness saw the car drive away.
I feel guilty about forgetting my friend's birthday.
He was not indicted by any real court, but he must now read to the children every Saturday.
